plaster.sheetLayout: user reference figure 1: a small render crop of a fine-speckled, matte, light warm-grey micro-cement/plaster inside corner. Perspective and studio lighting are baked into the pixels, so the pipeline derives the material from the evenly-lit top-face speckle patch instead of using the image as a flat PBR sheet.

limestone.sheetLayout: PBR sample sheet: sphere render top-left, large flat albedo sample top-right (x 628-1253, y 0-758); strip of six labelled 209 px channel patches (y 775-1040) with captions below (y 1059-1077); title band at the bottom. Captions are baked into the patch pixels.

satin.sheetLayout: user reference figure 2: a small render crop of a smooth, cool-grey satin surface with a crisp bright specular edge line. The line is lighting, not albedo, so only the flat lower-right region is used.

plaster.label: Plaster
plaster.tilePxNote: kept at 420 world px per tile: the top-face speckle patch is about 90 px across on the reference and the mirror-synthesised 1024 texture reads at a fine micro-cement grain at this density next to the limestone (480)
plaster.derivation: reference-derived (not a raw sheet crop): the evenly-lit top-face speckle patch [105,10,90,90] of plaster.png is flat-fielded (multi-scale low-frequency illumination removed), its fine speckle is restored with a deterministic micro-detail calibration (high-frequency component x4.0 around its local base, published as speckleBoost), colour-calibrated to a light warm-grey with mean luma 165 sRGB (per-channel gains published as colourGains), mirror-tiled 4x4 (seamless by construction) and Lanczos-resampled to 1024 px. The fine speckle is kept as the albedo micro-detail (deployed std about 8-11 levels after the SPEC rev4 4.2-A x0.60 detail compression). Normal / height are derived from the same wrap-consistent speckle field (subtle but visible micro-relief), roughness is a matte 0.92 with tiny speckle variation, metalness is 0 and ao is near-white with slight speckle darkening.

albedo.derivation: reference-derived (not a raw sheet crop): the evenly-lit top-face speckle patch [105,10,90,90] of plaster.png is flat-fielded (multi-scale low-frequency illumination removed), its fine speckle is restored with a deterministic micro-detail calibration (high-frequency component x4.0 around its local base, published as speckleBoost), colour-calibrated to a light warm-grey with mean luma 165 sRGB (per-channel gains published as colourGains), mirror-tiled 4x4 (seamless by construction) and Lanczos-resampled to 1024 px. The fine speckle is kept as the albedo micro-detail (deployed std about 8-11 levels after the SPEC rev4 4.2-A x0.60 detail compression). Normal / height are derived from the same wrap-consistent speckle field (subtle but visible micro-relief), roughness is a matte 0.92 with tiny speckle variation, metalness is 0 and ao is near-white with slight speckle darkening.
albedo.synthesis: flat-fielded top-face speckle patch mirror-tiled 4x4 then Lanczos-resampled to 1024 px; seamless by construction

normal.derivation: tangent-space OpenGL normal derived from the speckle relief field; very low relief (mean slope 0.0736)

roughness.derivation: matte plaster: mean 0.92 with subtle speckle variation

ao.derivation: near-white ambient occlusion with slight speckle darkening (mean 0.96)

tileability.note: mean absolute 8-bit channel delta across the wrap (0..1, lower is better), measured on the final deployed map; internalH/internalV are the mean adjacent-pixel deltas of the same map for reference. Limestone tiles are healed in output pixel space; the reference-derived materials are seamless by construction (even mirror tiling).

limestone.label: Limestone
limestone.tilePxNote: the large flat albedo sample is 626 px across; 480 px per tile keeps the fossil / crack scale between the plaster (420) and satin (260) groups
limestone.derivation: measured from the labelled PBR sample sheet limestone.png: albedo from the large flat sample (label-free), the other five channels from their own labelled strip patches; crops are label-free by assertion, seam-healed in output pixel space and level-calibrated (pattern untouched).

tileability.note: mean absolute 8-bit channel delta across the wrap (0..1, lower is better), measured on the final deployed map; internalH/internalV are the mean adjacent-pixel deltas of the same map for reference. Limestone tiles are healed in output pixel space; the reference-derived materials are seamless by construction (even mirror tiling).

satin.label: Satin
satin.tilePxNote: kept at 260 world px per tile so the smooth satin stays featureless at true scale and the specular response (not texture) defines the surface
satin.derivation: reference-derived (not a raw sheet crop): the flat lower-right region [85,88,67,26] of satin.png is used and the bright specular edge line is excluded (it is lighting, not albedo). The patch is flat-fielded, colour-calibrated to a cool grey with mean luma 150 sRGB, upscaled to a smooth 256 px base, mirror-tiled 4x4 (seamless by construction) to 1024 px - very low contrast, no grain and no periodic tile structure (albedo std below 1.5 levels). Normal/height are almost flat (mean normal slope below 0.01). Roughness is low (mean 0.30) and metalness high (mean 0.85) so the page studio softboxes produce the crisp specular edge highlight of the reference; ao is a flat near-white 247. Because the reference is grain-free, the data maps are near-uniform: their only variation is a deterministic C-infinity periodic field (fixed sum of integer-frequency sinusoids, exactly seamless) kept below 1.5 8-bit levels - not literal reference pixels, and deliberately not derived from the 67x26 patch, which would mirror-tile into visible rectangular cells.

albedo.derivation: reference-derived (not a raw sheet crop): the flat lower-right region [85,88,67,26] of satin.png is used and the bright specular edge line is excluded (it is lighting, not albedo). The patch is flat-fielded, colour-calibrated to a cool grey with mean luma 150 sRGB, upscaled to a smooth 256 px base, mirror-tiled 4x4 (seamless by construction) to 1024 px - very low contrast, no grain and no periodic tile structure (albedo std below 1.5 levels). Normal/height are almost flat (mean normal slope below 0.01). Roughness is low (mean 0.30) and metalness high (mean 0.85) so the page studio softboxes produce the crisp specular edge highlight of the reference; ao is a flat near-white 247. Because the reference is grain-free, the data maps are near-uniform: their only variation is a deterministic C-infinity periodic field (fixed sum of integer-frequency sinusoids, exactly seamless) kept below 1.5 8-bit levels - not literal reference pixels, and deliberately not derived from the 67x26 patch, which would mirror-tile into visible rectangular cells.
albedo.synthesis: flat lower-right patch (bright specular edge excluded) flat-fielded, resampled to a smooth 256 px base, mirror-tiled 4x4 to 1024 px; seamless by construction, very low contrast

normal.derivation: almost flat normal (mean slope 0.0001): smooth satin, no grain, gapless smooth variation field

roughness.derivation: low roughness: mean 0.30 with sub-level smooth periodic variation (no tile structure)

metalness.derivation: high metalness (mean 0.85, sub-level smooth variation) so the studio softboxes produce a crisp specular edge highlight like the reference

height.derivation: near-flat height (std 3.0 levels, mean 0.5): smooth, no grain, no tile structure

tileability.note: mean absolute 8-bit channel delta across the wrap (0..1, lower is better), measured on the final deployed map; internalH/internalV are the mean adjacent-pixel deltas of the same map for reference. Limestone tiles are healed in output pixel space; the reference-derived materials are seamless by construction (even mirror tiling).

pipeline.materialSetNote: SPEC Revision 5: three groups (plaster index 0, limestone index 1, satin index 2). The Revision 4 concrete and metal groups, their maps and their source copies were removed from the tree.
pipeline.referenceDerivationNote: plaster and satin are reference-derived from small user render crops (lighting/perspective baked in), not flat PBR sheets: the usable evenly-lit region is cropped, the low-frequency illumination is removed with a deterministic multi-scale flat field, colour is calibrated to the requested mean luma/chroma, and the result is mirror-tiled with even counts (outer edges identical, seamless by construction) and resampled. Normal/height/roughness/ao/metalness are derived from the same calibrated field as documented per channel.
pipeline.seamHealing: limestone tiles are cropped and healed in OUTPUT pixel space with an optimal wrap phase and a feather of real continuation pixels; plaster/satin are seamless by construction via even-count mirror tiling. Every map publishes measured wrap/internal deltas.
pipeline.normalConventionNote: all tangent-space normals are OpenGL (green = +Y, three.js r151 contract). Limestone normals are re-encoded from the sheet patch; plaster/satin normals are derived from their height fields with the OpenGL sign convention and are very low relief.
pipeline.colourSpaceNote: albedo PNGs are sRGB encoded; normal/roughness/metalness/ao/height PNGs are linear data maps.
pipeline.mapLevelNote: limestone roughness/ao levels are linearly calibrated to sensible ranges (pattern untouched); plaster/satin levels are calibrated to the material targets in SPEC Revision 5 section 5.1 (plaster matte roughness 0.92, metalness 0; satin roughness 0.30, metalness 0.85).
pipeline.detailCompressionNote: SPEC Revision 4 section 4.2-A is still applied: after all derivation and calibration, albedo / roughness / height deviations from their calibrated means are compressed by 0.60 / 0.75 / 0.70 (means preserved within 0.5 level) so the materials stay calm; factors are published in materials.<id>.detail and measured per channel in detailCompression.
